body.en:
Key terms:

  • Sewage: wastewater containing domestic and sometimes industrial wastewater and permitted infiltration.
  • Sewer: a pipe or conduit conveying sewage or stormwater; sewerage is the system of sewers and associated works.
  • Sullage/greywater: wastewater from baths, kitchens and washing, generally excluding toilet excreta; it can still contain pathogens and pollutants.
  • Sludge: solids separated or produced during wastewater treatment; effluent: liquid leaving a treatment stage.

Objectives: protect public health, prevent nuisance and environmental contamination, collect waste without unsafe human contact, and treat or reuse it in accordance with regulations. Untreated sewage must not be assumed safe for irrigation or discharge.
body.gu:
મુખ્ય terms:

  • Sewage: domestic અને ક્યારેક industrial wastewater તથા મંજૂર infiltration ધરાવતું wastewater.
  • Sewer: sewage અથવા stormwater વહન કરતો pipe અથવા conduit; sewerage એટલે sewers અને સંબંધિત works ની system.
  • Sullage/greywater: baths, kitchens અને washing નું wastewater, સામાન્ય રીતે toilet excreta વગર; તેમાં પણ pathogens અને pollutants હોઈ શકે.
  • Sludge: wastewater treatment માં અલગ પડેલા અથવા ઉત્પન્ન solids; effluent: treatment stage માંથી બહાર નીકળતું પ્રવાહી.

Objectives: public health નું રક્ષણ, nuisance અને environmental contamination અટકાવવું, અસલામત માનવીય સંપર્ક વગર waste એકત્ર કરવું અને regulations મુજબ treatment અથવા reuse કરવું. Untreated sewage ને irrigation અથવા discharge માટે safe માની ન લો.

body.en:
Historical conservancy system: human waste was collected from dry latrines or containers and transported separately. It has serious odour, infection, dignity and public-health problems. Manual scavenging and hazardous cleaning are prohibited under applicable Indian law; this historical description is not a recommendation.

Water-carriage system: water carries waste through traps, house drains and sewers to treatment and disposal or reuse. It requires reliable water, well-designed pipes, ventilation, treatment and safe maintenance. Where sewers are unavailable, safely managed onsite sanitation such as an appropriately designed septic system may be used, with treatment and regulated faecal-sludge management.

Collection networks: separate sewers carry sewage and stormwater in different pipes; combined systems carry both; partially separate systems admit selected stormwater. Selection depends on rainfall, topography, treatment capacity, cost and discharge requirements.
body.gu:
ઐતિહાસિક conservancy system: Dry latrines અથવા containers માંથી human waste એકત્ર કરી અલગ transport કરાતું. તેમાં ગંભીર odour, infection, dignity અને public-health સમસ્યાઓ છે. લાગુ ભારતીય કાયદા હેઠળ manual scavenging અને hazardous cleaning પ્રતિબંધિત છે; આ ઐતિહાસિક વર્ણન ભલામણ નથી.

Water-carriage system: પાણી waste ને traps, house drains અને sewers મારફતે treatment તથા disposal અથવા reuse સુધી લઈ જાય છે. તેમાં reliable water, યોગ્ય pipes, ventilation, treatment અને સલામત maintenance જરૂરી છે. Sewers ઉપલબ્ધ ન હોય તો યોગ્ય રીતે designed septic system જેવી safely managed onsite sanitation વાપરી શકાય, treatment અને નિયમિત faecal-sludge management સાથે.

Collection networks: Separate sewers માં sewage અને stormwater અલગ pipes માં વહે છે; combined system બંને સાથે વહન કરે છે; partially separate system પસંદ કરેલું stormwater સ્વીકારે છે. પસંદગી rainfall, topography, treatment capacity, cost અને discharge requirements પર આધારિત છે.

title.gu: Numerical 6.1 — Domestic wastewater flow નો અંદાજ

body.en:
Given: A community uses 1.0 MLD of domestic water. Assume 80% becomes sewage and infiltration adds 0.10 MLD. Estimate average sewage flow.

Step 1. Estimate sewage from domestic use.

Domestic sewage = 1.0 × 0.80Domestic sewage = 0.80 MLD

Step 2. Add assumed infiltration.

Total average flow = 0.80 + 0.10

Final answer:

Estimated average sewage flow = 0.90 MLD; actual return and infiltration vary.
body.gu:
આપેલ છે: Community 1.0 MLD domestic water વાપરે છે. તેમાંથી 80% sewage બને અને infiltration 0.10 MLD ઉમેરાય તેમ ધારો. Average sewage flow નો અંદાજ લો.

Step 1. Domestic use માંથી sewage ગણો.

Domestic sewage = 1.0 × 0.80Domestic sewage = 0.80 MLD

Step 2. ધારેલ infiltration ઉમેરો.

Total average flow = 0.80 + 0.10

અંતિમ જવાબ:

Estimated average sewage flow = 0.90 MLD; actual return અને infiltration બદલાય છે.

title.en: Formulae, methods and key data — Unit 6
title.gu: Formulae, methods અને key data — યુનિટ 6

body.en:
Return fraction and infiltration must be estimated for the actual area.

Average sewage flow = water use × return fraction + infiltration
body.gu:
Actual area માટે return fraction અને infiltration નો અંદાજ જરૂરી છે.

Average sewage flow = water use × return fraction + infiltration
